subject: Hosted API availability — customer impact summary & mitigation playbook (Navis)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Koval <elena.koval@navis.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API availability — brief impact summary

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the patience while we investigated the availability disruption across our hosted API in us-west-1 yesterday evening. I wanted to share a short impact summary so your team can plan any downstream communications and remediation steps on your side.

What happened (TL;DR):
- Between 2026-01-17 21:05 PST and 2026-01-18 01:30 PST we observed intermittent response elongation and a small set of 503 responses for generation endpoints that resulted from a prefetch/backpressure regression in the request fanout layer. The regression affected ~2.3% of requests for Navis during the window (higher for sustained batching workloads).

Customer impact:
- Short-lived elevated latency and occasional 503s for batch and streaming generation endpoints. No data loss observed; all requests either completed or returned explicit retryable errors.

What we did:
- Rolled back the routing change at 01:30 PST, increased backpressure headroom, and deployed a hotfix to the prefetch circuit at 02:10 PST.
- We also invalidated a stale KV-prefetch cache shard that amplified queueing for long-sequence requests.

Attachments: incident_log_summary.pdf (PDF) — short timeline, token-level metrics, and request-sample traces.

Next steps we propose:
1) We will provide a customer-facing mitigation playbook with suggested SDK retry settings and short-term guardrails (attached).
2) If you want, we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the traces and answer engineering questions.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts Navis' production workloads and we want to make this as actionable as possible.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Koval <elena.koval@navis.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@navis.io
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API availability — brief impact summary

Marissa — thanks for the update and the timeline. That matches what our SREs saw from the client side (spikes around 21:10–21:40 and then again ~00:50).

A couple of asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether any of the requests that returned 503s were billed as completed tokens? Our billing reconciliation flagged a few outliers and we want to align.
- Please include recommended short-term SDK retry/backoff settings — our SDK defaults are currently aggressive and we want to avoid client-side amplification.

Also looping in ops@navis.io for visibility.

Elena
Elena Koval
Head of Engineering, Navis

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Koval <elena.koval@navis.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API availability — brief impact summary

Elena — quick technical note:

- Billing: 503 responses were returned before token accounting was finalized, so customers were not billed for tokens on requests that returned 503. We've verified this against our token ledger for the Navis tenant and attached the reconciliation snippets to the incident_log_summary.pdf.

- Root cause summary (short): a routing change intended to reduce cold-start amplification introduced an edge condition where prefetch fanout could duplicate a fetch across two shards when a cache shard reported transient ETIMEDOUT. That duplicated the in-flight work and pushed a small subset of downstream workers into backpressure, increasing p95/p99 latency and some queue overflows that produced 503s.

- Immediate mitigations applied: rollback of routing change, eviction of the stale shard, and hotfix to de-duplicate prefetches in the fanout logic.

- Suggested customer SDK guardrails (short-term):
  * implement exponential backoff with jitter for 5xx responses: base 150ms, multiplier 2.0, max 3s
  * limit concurrent generation requests per client to 8 (for long-sequence workloads)
  * enable client-side idempotency tokens for retryable operations where applicable

I've added a short runbook to the shared drive with the traces and a list of internal actions (link below). If Navis wants our engineers to join a call to review traces, we can be available tomorrow 11:00–15:00 PST.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Koval <elena.koval@navis.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@navis.io
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Customer-facing mitigation playbook and credits next steps

Hi Elena — following up with the customer-facing materials and next steps.

Attached is a concise mitigation playbook (navis_customer_playbook.md) that includes:
- What happened (plain-language timeline)
- Immediate mitigation steps your engineers should apply (SDK settings + client guardrails)
- How to interpret failure modes vs. retryable errors
- Recommended monitoring thresholds (p95/p99) and alert playbooks

On credits and procurement: we do want to make the billing reconciliation straightforward. Per your ask, we confirm no billable tokens for requests that returned 503; we'll issue a small credit for the affected window as a good-faith gesture. Our finance team needs a PO or a short acceptance email to apply the credit — I included procurement@navis.io on this thread to coordinate.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please review the attached playbook and confirm if you'd like a 30-min review with Ben and our SREs (we can do today between 11:00–14:00 PST or tomorrow morning).
2) Procurement: please confirm the email/address for the credit application so we can escalate to finance.

Apologies again for the disruption. We'll follow up with a short postmortem within 72 hours that includes permanent remediation plans and any rollout schedule for the prefetch de-dup fix.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
(attachment: navis_customer_playbook.md)
From: Elena Koval <elena.koval@navis.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Customer-facing mitigation playbook and credits next steps

Laura — thanks for the playbook, that looks sensible and actionable. Ops has already applied the SDK guardrails for our batch workers and we saw p95 return to normal in our staging tests.

Procurement: procurement@navis.io here — please apply the credit to account NAV-2026-0042 and confirm when posted. We don't need a PO for this adjustment; an acceptance email is sufficient.

Also please include the short postmortem you mentioned when available — we'll share internally once we have that.

Appreciate the quick turnaround from the Redwood team.

— Elena
